4|job and can be swapped without touching the others. Import direction is

13|with `id`, `ch`, `n`, and `text`. `analysis.json` is the scene source

15|override, and the `final` emotion. `scenes.json` is the pipeline
16|intermediate that `analysis.json` mirrors. The reader consumes the book
17|fields, scene ranges and titles, and the `final` vector with intensity
18|and tempo. It never sees `jev`, `muse_override`, or provenance.
19|`core/reader.ts` defines `buildReaderModel`, which joins paragraphs to
20|scenes by ordinal range and throws on unordered scenes or on paragraphs
21|covered zero or two times.

26|false); `/` redirects to the first scene. The layout mounts the music
27|container once and passes slim metadata for all scenes: id, chapter,
28|and emotion triple only. Each scene page builds its view with
29|`buildSceneView` and ships only that scene's text, its chapter title,
30|and neighbor ids. Sub-pages come from `paginateScene` (250 words, split
31|at paragraph boundaries). The pager moves sub-pages in client state and
32|pushes routes with `router.push`, never `<Link>`; going back lands on
33|the previous scene's last sub-page through a one-shot client flag, never
34|a URL param, so prerendered pages stay static. The client never
35|receives other scenes' text, titles, or summaries. The progress line
36|reads `Chapter 1 · The Cyclone`, a spaced separator, then `Scene 1 of 4
37|· Page 1 of 3` as two spans on one line. Book type is 1.1875rem / 1.7

43|## Music library
44|
45|The library is a static `public/music/manifest.json`, version 3, fetched
46|by the client from `/music/manifest.json`. A static file needs no route,
47|ships from the CDN, and swaps by replacing files only. Tracks may be
48|several minutes long and are not loops unless marked so. A version 2
49|manifest migrates inline to one implicit `default` soundtrack of style
50|`orchestral`.

52|`MusicManifest = { version, styles, soundtracks, tracks, playlists }`.

55|optional `credit`. `Track = { id, src, title, emotion, vector,

57|`startSec` (default 0, where playback starts on first play and on each
58|loop), `endSec` (default the media end, where the track stops or loops),
59|`gainDb` (default 0, a loudness trim in dB, in -24..12),
60|`loop` (default true), `source` (`generated`, `jamendo`, or
61|`recording`), `artist`, `composer`, `license`, `attribution`, and
62|`sourceUrl` (https only). `durationSec` is the playable length: the
63|segment end (or the file end) minus `startSec`. `startSec` and `endSec`
64|are absolute media times with `startSec < endSec`; `endSec` stays within
65|`startSec + durationSec`. The player scales volume by the track gain and
66|ends or loops at `effectiveEnd`, the earlier of `endSec` and the loaded
67|media end. `emotion` is the hand label: one of the 8
68|emotion ids in `core/types.ts`. The vector covers the 8 ids with finite
69|entries in 0..1. Every track names a soundtrack id, every track style
70|matches its soundtrack style, and every style is a listed style id.
71|`core/music.ts` owns `parseManifest`, which rejects unknown versions,
72|duplicate ids, unknown soundtrack or style ids, style mismatches,
73|missing fields, bad vectors, NaN entries, out-of-range numbers,
74|a negative `startSec`, a bad `gainDb` or `endSec`, unknown `source`
75|values, a non-boolean
76|`playlistOnly`, and any `src`
77|that is not a `/music/` path or `https` URL. Unknown fields stay
78|ignored. A soundtrack with no
79|tracks parses. The reader calls it on every fetch, so a bad drop-in
80|fails loudly in dev. Remote audio lives on one Blob store, so
81|`media-src` in `next.config.ts` lists exactly
82|`https://3vuhzq2wmortnuxj.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`. Build the
83|manifest with `npm run build:music data/music/labels.json
84|data/music/library.json --out public/music/manifest.json`, which runs
85|`pipeline/labels-to-manifest.ts` and validates the result before
86|writing.
87|
88|`Track.playlistOnly` defaults to false. A true value marks a playlist
89|only track: it still names a soundtrack and style, but no emotion pick
90|ever returns it. `MusicManifest.playlists` holds
91|`Playlist = { id, label, trackIds }` entries, most notably
92|`just-play-chopin`. A missing key parses as an empty list, and a v2
93|migration gives an empty list. Parse rejects duplicate playlist ids,
94|empty labels, non-array `trackIds`, and any `trackIds` entry that names
95|no track, with the playlist and the id in the message.
96|
97|## Selection
98|
99|`MusicSelection = { style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick.
100|There is one mode only. Every scheduled select ranges over all tracks in
101|the current style and draws among the tracks with the scene emotion (or
102|the best same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within
103|`randomTolerance` (0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when
104|it is eligible, and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. The style is
105|the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The default style is
106|the first listed style with tracks; a stored style with tracks wins. The
107|session persists `{ style, volume, muted }` in localStorage under
108|`lectoria.music.v1`. Old values with `mode` or `soundtrackId` load by
109|`style` alone and ignore unknown fields; a stored object without
110|`volume` or `muted` loads `volume: null` and `muted: false`. A bad
111|`volume` (not a finite number in 0..1) loads null and the player starts
112|at 0.8; a bad `muted` loads false. A stored style with no tracks falls
113|back to the default. Storage exceptions never break playback. Dwell
114|and min-track rules hold. The core never calls `Math.random`; the
115|reader injects it and tests pass a seeded stub.
116|
117|## Next track and style change
118|
119|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order across the whole
120|style, wrapping and skipping the current, then the best same-style track
121|overall when the emotion is missing. A null scene cycles the style set
122|in id order. One track or none gives null.
123|
124|`requestStyleChange` picks the best match for the scene in the new style
125|by score. It never crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once
126|with the normal crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
127|mix toggle and no soundtrack-change button.
128|
129|## Playlist mode
130|
131|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
132|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
133|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
134|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
135|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
136|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
137|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
138|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
139|restored selection. The playlist is never persisted, so a reload returns
140|to emotion mode. The style selector stays disabled while it is on, and
141|the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
142|
143|## Similarity and config
144|
145|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
146|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
147|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
148|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
149|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
150|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
151|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
152|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
153|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
154|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
155|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
156|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
157|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
158|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
159|and overrides are unchanged.
160|
161|## Selection scheduler
162|
163|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
164|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
165|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
166|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
167|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
168|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
169|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
170|with the scene it belongs to.
171|
172|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
173|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
174|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
175|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
176|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
177|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
178|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
179|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
180|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
181|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
182|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
183|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
184|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
185|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
186|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
187|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
188|skip override.
189|
190|## Player
191|
192|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
193|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
194|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
195|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
196|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
197|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
198|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
199|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
200|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
201|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
202|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
203|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
204|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
205|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
206|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
207|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
208|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
209|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
210|
211|The bar is one sticky row, 56 px tall: the `Lectoria` wordmark left,
212|the player centre, the Chopin button and the source icon link right.
213|The inner row is centered with 24 px side padding, one bottom hairline
214|in the border token, and nothing touching the viewport edges. The inner
215|max-width is 56rem, wider than the 65ch book column on purpose so the
216|full now-playing line fits at 1280 px. The player holds Previous,
217|Play/Pause, Next, the now-playing line (flexible space, `min-width`
218|16rem, truncated with an ellipsis, full line in the `title` tooltip),
219|a mute icon button (`aria-pressed`, `aria-label` `Mute` / `Unmute`, the
220|icon shows the muted state), a volume slider with `aria-label` `Volume`
221|(96 px) next to it, a style selector with `aria-label`
222|`Orchestra / Piano` and no visible label text listing only styles that
223|have tracks (hidden while fewer than two qualify), then the Chopin
224|button and the source icon link. The transport and mute buttons and the
225|source icon link are icon-only inline SVGs (`currentColor`, 32 px hit
226|area), quiet and neutral, Meta blue on hover and focus-visible, each
227|with `aria-label` and `title`; the source link reads `Music source
228|(opens in new tab)`. Previous walks the session history and restarts
229|the current track with no history, including the current playlist piece
230|in playlist mode; Next cycles same-emotion tracks in the style.
231|A `Just play Chopin` round image button (`/art/chopin-just-play-me.png`,
232|40 px, `alt` and `aria-label` `Just play Chopin`) appears only when
233|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; it carries
234|`aria-pressed`, and while pressed it shows a 2 px Meta-blue ring plus
235|scale 1.05. The now-playing line shows `display title · composer
236|· source`: `displayTitle` drops quoted nicknames, key phrases, and
237|opus/catalogue suffixes from the track title, and the source is the
238|artist plus ` / <platform>` when the attribution names Musopen or
239|Jamendo and the artist does not already say it, dropped when it would
240|repeat the performer. The full manifest title plus the license and full
241|attribution sits in the `title` tooltip. On manifest failure the reader
242|still renders and the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays
243|under 200 ms. Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible
244|focus, and keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine,
245|transport, and bar layout; `app/player-controls.tsx` holds the style
246|selector and the playlist toggle; `app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage
247|helper. The heading keeps `h2:focus:not(:focus-visible){outline:none}`
248|so mouse navigation shows no box while keyboard focus keeps its ring.
249|No user-visible emotion labels exist; ids stay as they are.
250|`core/music-credit.ts` builds the line as a pure function with tests,
251|including the pure `displayTitle`.
252|`core/music-history.ts` is the bounded history stack and
253|`requestManualTrack` in `core/music-schedule.ts` holds a manual pick.
254|
255|## Image api
256|
257|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
258|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
259|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
260|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
261|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
262|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic English message.
263|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Illustrate
264|scene" uses the scene id from the route.
265|
266|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
267|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
268|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
269|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
270|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
271|friendly English message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
272|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
273|
274|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
275|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
276|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
277|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
278|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
279|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
280|and backfills the index.
281|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
282|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
283|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
284|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
285|quota and budget and release the lock.
286|
287|## Chat api
288|
289|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
290|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
291|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
292|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
293|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
294|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
295|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
296|
297|## Quotas and budget
298|
299|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
300|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
301|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
302|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
303|the client, details stay in server logs.

96|
97|## Selection
98|
99|`MusicSelection = { style }` is the session: `style` scopes every pick.
100|There is one mode only. Every scheduled select ranges over all tracks in
101|the current style and draws among the tracks with the scene emotion (or
102|the best same-style tracks when the emotion is missing) within
103|`randomTolerance` (0.05) of the best score, keeps the current track when
104|it is eligible, and avoids an immediate repeat otherwise. The style is
105|the user's choice, changed with the style selector. The default style is
106|the first listed style with tracks; a stored style with tracks wins. The
107|session persists `{ style, volume, muted }` in localStorage under
108|`lectoria.music.v1`. Old values with `mode` or `soundtrackId` load by
109|`style` alone and ignore unknown fields; a stored object without
110|`volume` or `muted` loads `volume: null` and `muted: false`. A bad
111|`volume` (not a finite number in 0..1) loads null and the player starts
112|at 0.8; a bad `muted` loads false. A stored style with no tracks falls
113|back to the default. Storage exceptions never break playback. Dwell
114|and min-track rules hold. The core never calls `Math.random`; the
115|reader injects it and tests pass a seeded stub.
116|
117|## Next track and style change
118|
119|`nextTrack` cycles same-emotion tracks in score order across the whole
120|style, wrapping and skipping the current, then the best same-style track
121|overall when the emotion is missing. A null scene cycles the style set
122|in id order. One track or none gives null.
123|
124|`requestStyleChange` picks the best match for the scene in the new style
125|by score. It never crosses styles. The scheduler applies it at once
126|with the normal crossfade and holds the choice like a Next. There is no
127|mix toggle and no soundtrack-change button.
128|
129|## Playlist mode
130|
131|`SchedulerState.playlist` holds `{ id, index }` while a fixed playlist
132|plays. `enterPlaylist` switches at once to the first `trackIds` entry
133|with `crossfadeSec`, no dwell and no min-track rule. While it is on,
134|scene changes update the active scene but never switch, `requestNext`
135|and `noteTrackEnded` advance to the next entry in order and wrap from
136|the last to the first, and playlist tracks run to their end because the
137|player forces looping off. `exitPlaylist` clears the playlist state and
138|switches at once to the best match for the current scene under the
139|restored selection. The playlist is never persisted, so a reload returns
140|to emotion mode. The style selector stays disabled while it is on, and
141|the style list hides styles with only playlist tracks.
142|
143|## Similarity and config
144|
145|`Similarity = (scene, track, weights) => number`, where
146|`SceneSignal = { vector, intensity, tempo }`. The default is
147|`bhattacharyyaSimilarity`: both 8-emotion vectors renormalize to sum 1
148|(an all-zero vector gives an affinity of 0), `E` is the sum of
149|`sqrt(s_k * t_k)`, and the score is `weights.emotion * E` plus
150|`weights.intensity` and `weights.tempo` each for intensity and tempo
151|closeness. Scoring and ranking pass the resolved config weights in, so
152|a weights override changes the ranking. `cosineSimilarity` over
153|`buildFeatures` output stays as an exported alternative. One exported object,
154|`MUSIC_CONFIG`, holds `similarity`, `weights`, `switchMargin` (0.07),
155|`dwellSec` (20), `minTrackSec` (45), `hardCutMargin` (0.20),
156|`crossfadeSec` (3), and `hardCutCrossfadeSec` (1.5). Everything else
157|reads from it. Ranking ties go to the lower track id. Route entries use
158|`sceneEntryDwellSec` (5) as the dwell override; scoring, hysteresis,
159|and overrides are unchanged.
160|
161|## Selection scheduler
162|
163|`core/music-schedule.ts` is a pure state machine. The reader calls
164|`observeScene`, `tickScheduler`, `requestNext`, and `noteTrackEnded`
165|with explicit `nowSec` values, so all timing is testable without
166|timers. The reader cues music on scene entry only: one `observeScene`
167|call per route id, gated by an id comparison, so sub-page moves never
168|reach the scheduler. State holds the current track id and when it started, the active
169|scene id, the pending scene id and since when, and the skip override
170|with the scene it belongs to.
171|
172|A newly entered scene becomes pending and the dwell clock restarts, so
173|fast scrolling keeps only the newest scene. The first track ever plays
174|at once with no dwell. After the pending scene holds for `dwellSec` it
175|becomes active and the override clears. Then the best track switches in
176|only when it beats the current score by `switchMargin` and the current
177|track played `minTrackSec`, unless it wins by `hardCutMargin` (hard
178|cut, short fade). A second passes the active scene back through the
179|switch check, so a hold from `minTrackSec` releases on time, unless a
180|skip override stands: ticks return no change while it is set, and only
181|a new scene promotion clears it. A switch
182|reports its crossfade length: 3 s normally,
183|1.5 s for hard cuts. The skip choice holds until the next scene change;
184|after that, dwell and hysteresis apply with the override track as the
185|current track. A null scene means a failed analysis with no vector, so
186|it never triggers a switch. A non-looping track that ends fades into
187|the best remaining track, excluding the one that ended, and clears the
188|skip override.
189|
190|## Player
191|
192|`app/player.tsx` takes the track, the fade length for the latest switch,
193|the scene title, a skip flag, and callbacks. It owns two `audio`
194|elements, play state, volume, and the equal-power crossfade
195|(cos/sin gains over the fade time, driven by `requestAnimationFrame`).
196|It never uses the `loop` attribute. Volume lives in a ref, so the slider
197|never re-runs the track effect or touches `src`. A new track request
198|mid-fade cancels the pending fade and fades from the audible element to
199|the newest track. On load each track seeks to `startSec` once metadata
200|is available. Long tracks with `loop` true crossfade into the other
201|element playing the same track from `startSec` when `currentTime`
202|reaches `duration - fade`, where `fade` is the latest scheduler fade
203|length, or the config `crossfadeSec` when none was reported yet. When
204|`loop` is false the player reports the end and the scheduler picks the
205|next-best track excluding the ended one. Pause stops both elements and
206|freezes the fade in place; play resumes the audible elements from the
207|frozen point. Audio starts once, on the first press, with fade 0.
208|Audio starts only after the user presses play. Reduced motion is read in
209|state with a change listener and affects visuals only, never the fade.
210|
211|The bar is one sticky row, 56 px tall: the `Lectoria` wordmark left,
212|the player centre, the Chopin button and the source icon link right.
213|The inner row is centered with 24 px side padding, one bottom hairline
214|in the border token, and nothing touching the viewport edges. The inner
215|max-width is 56rem, wider than the 65ch book column on purpose so the
216|full now-playing line fits at 1280 px. The player holds Previous,
217|Play/Pause, Next, the now-playing line (flexible space, `min-width`
218|16rem, truncated with an ellipsis, full line in the `title` tooltip),
219|a mute icon button (`aria-pressed`, `aria-label` `Mute` / `Unmute`, the
220|icon shows the muted state), a volume slider with `aria-label` `Volume`
221|(96 px) next to it, a style selector with `aria-label`
222|`Orchestra / Piano` and no visible label text listing only styles that
223|have tracks (hidden while fewer than two qualify), then the Chopin
224|button and the source icon link. The transport and mute buttons and the
225|source icon link are icon-only inline SVGs (`currentColor`, 32 px hit
226|area), quiet and neutral, Meta blue on hover and focus-visible, each
227|with `aria-label` and `title`; the source link reads `Music source
228|(opens in new tab)`. Previous walks the session history and restarts
229|the current track with no history, including the current playlist piece
230|in playlist mode; Next cycles same-emotion tracks in the style.
231|A `Just play Chopin` round image button (`/art/chopin-just-play-me.png`,
232|40 px, `alt` and `aria-label` `Just play Chopin`) appears only when
233|the manifest defines that playlist with tracks; it carries
234|`aria-pressed`, and while pressed it shows a 2 px Meta-blue ring plus
235|scale 1.05. The now-playing line shows `display title · composer
236|· source`: `displayTitle` drops quoted nicknames, key phrases, and
237|opus/catalogue suffixes from the track title, and the source is the
238|artist plus ` / <platform>` when the attribution names Musopen or
239|Jamendo and the artist does not already say it, dropped when it would
240|repeat the performer. The full manifest title plus the license and full
241|attribution sits in the `title` tooltip. On manifest failure the reader
242|still renders and the bar shows a short neutral note. UI motion stays
243|under 200 ms. Controls are real buttons and inputs with labels, visible
244|focus, and keyboard use. `app/player.tsx` keeps the audio engine,
245|transport, and bar layout; `app/player-controls.tsx` holds the style
246|selector and the playlist toggle; `app/music-prefs.ts` owns the storage
247|helper. The heading keeps `h2:focus:not(:focus-visible){outline:none}`
248|so mouse navigation shows no box while keyboard focus keeps its ring.
249|No user-visible emotion labels exist; ids stay as they are.
250|`core/music-credit.ts` builds the line as a pure function with tests,
251|including the pure `displayTitle`.
252|`core/music-history.ts` is the bounded history stack and
253|`requestManualTrack` in `core/music-schedule.ts` holds a manual pick.
254|
255|## Image api
256|
257|`POST /api/images` (Node runtime, `maxDuration` 120). Request is a
258|discriminated union: `{ kind: "passage", bookId, textVersion, n }` names
259|the paragraph where the selection starts, `{ kind: "scene", bookId,
260|textVersion, sceneId }` names the scene. Validation is strict: known
261|book, matching `textVersion`, integer `n` inside the book, known
262|`sceneId`. Any other body is a 400 with a generic English message.
263|The client sends ordinals and ids only, never text. "Illustrate
264|scene" uses the scene id from the route.
265|
266|Responses (typed in `core/types.ts`): `{ status: "ready", url, cached,
267|caption }` with a Vercel Blob URL, never bytes; `{ status: "pending" }`
268|when another request holds the lock, in which case the client reposts
269|every 3 s up to about 2 minutes; `{ status: "error", code, message }`
270|where code is `quota`, `budget`, `unavailable`, or `bad_request` with a
271|friendly English message. Caption is the scene title for scenes and the
272|first words of the paragraph for passages, built server-side.
273|
274|The passage cache key is book plus start paragraph plus `textVersion`
275|plus `PROMPT_VERSION` (`v1`); the scene key is book plus scene id plus
276|the same versions. Both map to a deterministic Blob path
277|(`addRandomSuffix: false`, `allowOverwrite: false`). An Upstash Redis
278|index maps key to Blob URL, so hits are one GET; on an index miss the
279|server lists by exact path prefix (head equivalent) before generating
280|and backfills the index.
281|A Redis lock per key returns `pending` to concurrent requests. Quota is
282|5 new images per person per day by hashed IP and signed cookie,
283|whichever runs out first; a shared spend counter in integer
284|micro-dollars sits under `SPEND_CAP_USD` (default 10). Failures refund
285|quota and budget and release the lock.
286|
287|## Chat api
288|
289|Contract only, no routes. Request `{ bookId, textVersion, positionN,
290|spoilerMode, messages }` carries the chat history and the reader
291|position. The response is streamed text. The server builds context from
292|the book text up to `positionN`, or the whole book when `spoilerMode` is
293|on, with the book prefix first and the question last so readers share
294|the prompt cache. The system prompt answers only from that text and
295|refuses the rest. Types live in `core/types.ts`.
296|
297|## Quotas and budget
298|
299|Server only. Spend is counted in integer micro-dollars: reserve with
300|Redis `INCRBY` before each model call, refund with `DECRBY` after, one
301|reserve per call including retries. The server clamps every model tool
302|argument. Clients never see keys or raw errors. Generic messages go to
303|the client, details stay in server logs.
